national_raw_news.content: External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar today lauded the successful conclusion of BRICS Summit 2026 in New Delhi, saying that the world saw the strong convening power of India, as most of the heads of state were present to represent their countries. Talking to the media, Dr Jaishankar said that it is important to recognise that this BRICS summit was taking place in a very polarised world, where there are two major conflicts and very strong opinions and interests. He said that all countries were able to get out a statement urging peace, security, stability, long-term understanding, the smooth flow of global trade, supply chains, energy, and of the protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure. Dr Jaishankar informed that there were 32 delegations that had come from 11 member states, 10 partner states, four regional organisations and seven international organisations. He said that, even in the midst of this polarisation, a consensus was forged on the toughest issue of the day, which was the West Asia conflict. The Minister stated that the BRICS countries were very clear that any act of terrorism is a criminal act, and it also explicitly recognised the unacceptability of the Pahalgam attack. Condemning the terrorism, Dr Jaishankar said that BRICS emphasised zero tolerance for terrorism and rejected double standards in countering it.

national_raw_news.title: 50 mins ago | National 29 Global leaders praise BRICS Summit under India’s chairmanship
national_raw_news.content: India’s leadership of BRICS has won praise from several member countries following the successful conclusion of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi. The two-day summit, held in the National Capital under India’s chairmanship, concluded yesterday. BRICS comprises 11 major emerging economies, representing nearly half the world’s population and around 40 per cent of global GDP. The BRICS countries unanimously adopted the New Delhi Declaration 2026 at the Summit on Saturday, with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping among the world leaders attending. The New Delhi Declaration also commended India’s chairship and expressed appreciation to the Government and people of India for hosting the summit. South Africa, Russia, China, Brazil, and the United Arab Emirates, welcomed India’s efforts to strengthen cooperation within the grouping and advance the priorities of the Global South. South African President Cyril Ramaphosa praised India’s leadership as BRICS chair, saying New Delhi hosted a very successful summit and managed to bring member countries together to adopt the New Delhi Declaration despite doubts over reaching consensus. He said, the successful adoption of the declaration was a result of collective efforts by all BRICS members, while congratulating India for its organisation and leadership. China’s state media and leadership hailed the New Delhi Declaration as a positive step for higher-quality cooperation and solidarity among Global South nations. On the declaration, Russia reaffirmed Moscow’s dedication to an inclusive, development-oriented partnership with BRICS partner countries. Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs in a social media post, reiterated Moscow’s commitment to strengthening Multilateralism and Multipolarity, to upholding international law, including the Purposes and Principles of the UN Charter in their entirety. Uruguay’s Foreign Minister Mario Lubetkin said, BRICS New Delhi Declaration addresses the core needs of the Global South and provides a practical framework for tackling shared global challenges. In an exclusive interaction with a news agency, Mr Lubetkin said issues such as environmental stability, peace, geopolitical pressures, trade and artificial intelligence affect countries across regions, making the outcomes of the BRICS Summit relevant well beyond the grouping. He said the declaration successfully captured the priorities of participating leaders and described it as a useful and practical framework for addressing common challenges. UN Chief António Guterres praised India’s BRICS Presidency and congratulated Prime Minister Narendra Modi on India holding the BRICS chairship for the fourth time. The World Health Organisation (WHO) also praised the New Delhi Declaration. In a social media post, the Director General of the World Health Organisation, Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, appreciated the commitment to universal health coverage, resilient health systems, and the successful conclusion of negotiations on the Pathogen Access and Benefit Sharing Annex to the Pandemic Agreement. Mr Ghebreyesus also praised the efforts of BRICS countries to end Tuberculosis (TB), strengthen the health workforce, digital health, integrate traditional medicine, and deliver health for all. He also expressed gratitude towards Prime Minister Narendra Modi for the warm welcome at the summit. A US-based analyst has described India’s hosting of the 18th BRICS Summit as a success, saying the substantive New Delhi Declaration reflects New Delhi’s ability to build consensus among countries with differing views. Michael Kugelman, a Senior Fellow for South Asia at the Atlantic Council, said the declaration reflects India’s growing convening power and the increasing appeal of the BRICS grouping. The declaration expressed serious concern over unilateral tariff and non-tariff measures, saying they distort global trade and violate World Trade Organisation rules. It also stressed the need for cooperation on terrorism, conflict prevention and the peaceful resolution of disputes. Mr Kugelman said the declaration seeks to boost trade among BRICS nations and strengthen the grouping as an alternative to Western-led economic and financial institutions. He added that the push for greater intra-BRICS trade showed the bloc’s ability to deliver substantive measures for economies facing tariffs and sanctions linked to the Trump administration’s trade policies. During its year-long chairship, India focused on strengthening economic and development cooperation, promoting the interests of developing countries and giving greater voice to the Global South in global affairs.

national_raw_news.title: 54 mins ago | International 14 Human Rights Council of PoJK expresses concern over prolonged protests and unrest in region
national_raw_news.content: The Human Rights Council of Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir has expressed concern over prolonged protests and unrest in the region, particularly in Rawalakot and the districts of Poonch and Sudhnooti. The rights body said the demonstrations have now completed 100 days, creating uncertainty and affecting the wider region. It warned that any further delay in meaningful dialogue could deepen public frustration, mistrust and instability. The council has urged the Pakistani authorities and all concerned stakeholders to begin immediate and result-oriented talks, exercise restraint and pursue a peaceful and democratic resolution. In a separate statement, the council raised concern over the arrest of Javed Arif Abbasi, a member of the District Council in Bagh. It said peacefully raising issues related to public rights is a fundamental democratic right. The council called for any charges against Abbasi to be dealt with through a transparent legal process, and said he should be released without delay if there are no clear legal grounds for his detention. The rights body said differences of opinion should be addressed through dialogue and the law, rather than through arrest or pressure. The Human Rights Council PoJK is an independent, non-governmental and non-profit human rights organisation focused on protecting human dignity.

national_raw_news.title: India wins record eighth Women’s Asia Cup title, President Murmu congratulates team 15 hours ago 510
national_raw_news.content: India produced a commanding all-round performance to defeat Sri Lanka by 72 runs in the Women’s Asia Cup 2026 final in Dubai last night, securing a record-extending eighth Asia Cup title. The victory also helped India avenge their defeat to Sri Lanka in the 2024 final. It was India’s sixth win over Sri Lanka in an Asia Cup final across the ODI and T20 formats, including the 2004 edition when India defeated Sri Lanka 5-0 in the two-team tournament. India first posted a formidable 183 for 5 after openers Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana produced a record-breaking 129-run partnership. The bowlers then completed the job by dismissing Sri Lanka for 111 in 19.4 overs, with Shree Charani taking four wickets and Deepti Sharma claiming three. Shafali Verma was declared Player of the Match. India’s victory was built on a combination of explosive batting at the top and disciplined bowling through the middle and final overs. The record partnership between Shafali and Mandhana gave India the platform, while Charani and Deepti dismantled Sri Lanka’s chase to seal a memorable eighth title. President Droupadi Murmu, Vice President C P Radhakrishnan and Prime Minister Narendra Modi congratulated all the members of Team India on winning Women’s T20 Asia Cup Championship 2026. In a social media post, the President said that the players played superbly as a team throughout the tournament, winning all the matches and making the country proud. She said that these players are a source of great inspiration for the youth of the country. She also expressed confidence that the team will script many more inspiring chapters of success and excellence. Vice President C P Radhakrishnan also congratulated the team on lifting the Women’s T20 Asia Cup for a record eighth time. He said that the team’s unbeaten campaign, exceptional teamwork and unwavering determination throughout the tournament have brought immense pride to the nation. He also wished the players well for their future endeavours. Prime Minister Modi said that the confidence, consistency and remarkable spirit of the players were on full display throughout the tournament. Congratulating the Women’s team, Mr Modi wished that this triumph inspire millions of youngsters across the country to play more and shine. Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla has congratulated the Indian women’s cricket team via a social media post. Mr Birla lauded the team for remaining unbeaten throughout the tournament and securing victory in the Asia Cup for the 8th time. He added that the cricketers gave a splendid demonstration of their talent and determination in the tournament and this victory is a triumph of the strength, hard work, and dreams of the daughters of India. The Lok Sabha Speaker emphasised that the accomplishment inspires the youth of the country, to dream big, work hard, and move forward with full determination to achieve their goals.

national_raw_news.title: Tripura govt to organise series of programmes under Seva Sankalp Abhiyan 1 hour ago 20
national_raw_news.content: The Tripura government will organise a series of programmes across the state to mark Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s birthday. The month-long campaign will begin on September 17, the Prime Minister’s birthday, and continue until October 17. Addressing a press conference at the Secretariat today, Chief Minister Dr. Manik Saha said the campaign will be held under the theme “Seva Sankalp Abhiyan – Jan Seva Hi Prabhu Seva”. The programmes will also highlight Prime Minister Modi’s 25 years of continuous public service, including his nearly 13-year tenure as Gujarat Chief Minister and his service as Prime Minister since 2014. The Chief Minister highlighted initiatives such as Jan Dhan Yojana, PM Gati Shakti, Ujjwala Yojana, Operation Sindoor and the abrogation of Article 370. Programmes including Angan Milan Seva, Seva Ki Kahani, Kalash Yatra, Service My Contribution, Seva Ke Rang-Rashtra Ke Sang, Sushasan Samvad and Namo Seva Ankahi Kahaniyan will be organised across Tripura. Several committees have been formed to ensure the successful implementation of the campaign. The Information and Cultural Affairs Department has been designated as the nodal department, while ministers and secretaries have been assigned responsibilities for different programmes. Information and Cultural Affairs Secretary Abhishek Singh was also present at the press conference.

national_raw_news.title: BJP secures overall lead in Rajasthan urban local body elections 2 hours ago 75
national_raw_news.content: In Rajasthan, the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party got an overall lead in the urban local body elections held across the state. Counting of votes took place today for 10,245 wards across the state. The urban local bodies include 10 municipal corporations, 47 municipal councils and 252 municipalities. The BJP has secured a clear majority in the municipal corporations of Jaipur, Kota, Udaipur and Bhilwara, while leading in Alwar. In Bikaner, the Congress has secured a clear majority, while the party is also leading in Ajmer and Pali. In Bharatpur, Independents have registered a major victory, winning 38 of the 65 wards. In Jodhpur Municipal Corporation, both the BJP and Congress have won 44 seats each out of 100. Among the 47 municipal councils, the BJP got lead in 21, while the Congress is ahead in 17. Similarly, of the 252 municipalities, the BJP has won 144, while the Congress has secured victory in 92. Speaking to reporters, Chief Minister Bhajan Lal Sharma said that the people had expressed their confidence in Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the performance of the state government. He described the results as the people’s endorsement of the present state government’s two-and-a-half-year tenure. Meanwhile, president of Rajasthan Pradesh Congress Committee Govind Singh Dotasra said that despite the BJP putting in its full strength in the elections, it had failed to secure the mandate it had expected. Polling for the 309 urban local bodies were held in two phases on September 9 and 11. BJP today said that the party is inching towards a spectacular victory in the local bodies elections in Rajasthan. Addressing a press conference in New Delhi, BJP Spokesperson Dr Sudhanshu Trivedi said that in 9 out 10 municipal corporations, the BJP along with its allies are placed in a comfortable position. The BJP Spokesperson further said that the Congress party’s policy of conducting elections in 8 phases and dividing Jaipur, Jodhpur and Kota municipal corporations has been rejected by the people, whereas the BJP conducted the elections in one phase. He said that this victory demonstrates that the Congress party’s claims contain more propaganda and less reality.
